results.note: None-vs-truthiness: a run whose start is falsy would be silently dropped instead of closed, merging a free run across an occupied cell.
Run start anchored to the block start rather than the current row: every run after an occupied cell is written at the wrong offset.
Dropped tail flush: the final run is never emitted, so nothing is written.
Off-by-one: the last data row is never considered for a marker.
and/or swap on the covered classification: marked_rows is empty and the report lies about what was written.
Boundary flip: a single-data-row sheet (last == first) skips the occupancy check and the update entirely.
Inverted force guard: the overwrite-protection read only happens WITH --force, so the default path destroys occupied marker formulas.
Off-by-one on the span end: each written range claims one row more than it has values for.
Comparison widened: every run renders as a single-cell A1 ref regardless of length.
Dropped FORMULA render option: a live marker formula evaluating to "" reads as empty and the write destroys it.
Fail-open on an unreadable column: the whole block is overwritten blind.
Dropped bound on the returned rows: rows past the block are marked occupied.
Dropped normalization: a whitespace-only cell counts as occupied.
and/or swap in run condensing: cells in different columns get merged into one span.
Comparison flip: single cells print as "L5:L5" and real runs collapse to their head.
Inverted early return: skips are never reported and an empty plan prints a bogus zero-skip line.
Removed the skip report on the real-write path.
Default flipped on the overwrite option: a context that does not carry force overwrites occupied marker cells.
